tools.title: Freelance Hourly Rate Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Use this guide to estimate an hourly billing rate from your desired annual take-home income, business costs, tax reserve and expected billable time. The result is a planning estimate, not a tax assessment or a guarantee of work.

steps.title: Enter your income goal
steps.body: Enter the annual take-home income you want after setting aside the estimated tax reserve.

steps.title: Add annual business costs
steps.body: Include the annual operating costs that must be covered by your freelance revenue.

steps.title: Set the tax reserve and billable time
steps.body: Enter a tax-reserve percentage below 100%, billable hours per week and working weeks per year. Exclude unpaid administration time unless it is included in your hours.

steps.title: Review the estimated hourly rate
steps.body: The calculator estimates annual billable hours, gross revenue needed and the hourly rate required to meet the entered targets.

sections.heading: How the estimate is calculated
sections.body: Annual billable hours = billable hours per week × working weeks. Annual revenue target = (desired take-home income + annual business costs) ÷ (1 − tax-reserve rate). Hourly billing rate = annual revenue target ÷ annual billable hours.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: The tax reserve is a percentage assumption, not a jurisdiction-specific tax calculation. Actual tax obligations, unpaid work, leave, late payments and demand can change the rate you need.

tools.title: Profit Margin Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Use this calculator to compare revenue with costs and understand both profit margin and markup. Enter revenue and costs for the same currency and reporting period.

steps.title: Enter revenue
steps.body: Enter total sales or revenue for the period.

steps.title: Enter total costs
steps.body: Enter the costs associated with the same period and currency.

steps.title: Calculate profit and percentages
steps.body: The calculator subtracts costs from revenue, then calculates margin and markup when their denominators are non-zero.

steps.title: Review the result
steps.body: A negative profit or margin means costs exceed revenue. A percentage is undefined when its denominator is zero.

sections.heading: Formulas
sections.body: Profit = revenue − costs. Profit margin (%) = profit ÷ revenue × 100. Markup on cost (%) = profit ÷ costs × 100.

sections.heading: Margin versus markup
sections.body: Margin expresses profit as a share of revenue. Markup expresses profit relative to cost; the two percentages use different denominators.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: This is a simple arithmetic comparison. It does not classify costs, account for tax, or determine whether revenue and costs have been recorded under an appropriate accounting method.

tools.title: Mortgage Affordability Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Estimate a possible home-price range using gross monthly income, existing debt payments, down payment, mortgage terms and recurring housing costs. This estimate is not a lender approval or borrowing offer.

steps.title: Enter household income and debts
steps.body: Use gross monthly household income and existing monthly debt payments.

steps.title: Enter down payment and loan terms
steps.body: Provide the available down payment, annual mortgage rate and loan term.

steps.title: Include recurring housing costs
steps.body: Enter monthly property tax, home insurance and HOA or similar fees.

steps.title: Set affordability ratios
steps.body: Review the debt-to-income and housing-cost ratios used by the estimate.

steps.title: Calculate the housing budget
steps.body: The calculator uses the lower of the entered housing-cost limit and debt-based limit, not below zero.

steps.title: Review the estimated home price
steps.body: Taxes, insurance and HOA are deducted to estimate principal-and-interest capacity; the supported loan amount is combined with the down payment.

sections.heading: How the estimate works
sections.body: The housing-cost cap is gross monthly income × housing ratio. The debt cap is gross monthly income × maximum DTI − existing monthly debts. The lower non-negative amount is the estimated housing budget. Monthly tax, insurance and HOA costs are subtracted before calculating the supported loan amount.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: Other ownership costs may not be included unless entered. Lenders may use different underwriting rules, income treatment, credit criteria, reserves and rate assumptions. This calculator does not provide preapproval.

tools.title: Mortgage Payoff and Extra Payment Guide
tools.introduction: Compare a standard mortgage repayment schedule with a scenario that adds an extra monthly amount toward principal. The comparison assumes the same rate and remaining term for both schedules.

steps.title: Enter the current balance
steps.body: Use the outstanding mortgage principal, not the original amount borrowed.

steps.title: Enter the rate and remaining term
steps.body: Provide the annual interest rate and remaining repayment term.

steps.title: Add an extra monthly amount
steps.body: Enter the additional amount you expect to pay each month. The model assumes it reduces principal.

steps.title: Calculate both schedules
steps.body: The calculator compares the standard payment with the accelerated payment and models monthly interest and balances.

steps.title: Compare interest and payoff time
steps.body: Review estimated interest saved and months saved against the standard schedule.

sections.heading: Monthly calculation
sections.body: Monthly interest = opening balance × annual interest rate ÷ 1,200. The accelerated scenario adds the extra amount to the standard payment and applies it toward principal.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: The model assumes the extra amount is applied to principal each month. Confirm your lender's payment-allocation rules, prepayment limits, fees and timing before relying on an estimate.

tools.title: Mortgage Refinance Comparison Guide
tools.introduction: Compare the estimated payment and interest on your current mortgage with a refinance scenario that includes estimated closing costs. Different loan terms can change the overall comparison.

steps.title: Enter the current mortgage
steps.body: Provide the outstanding balance, current annual rate and remaining term.

steps.title: Enter the refinance terms
steps.body: Provide the proposed annual rate and new loan term.

steps.title: Add closing costs
steps.body: Enter estimated closing costs; this model adds them to the refinanced loan balance.

steps.title: Compare monthly payments
steps.body: Review the current payment, proposed payment and their difference.

steps.title: Review break-even and interest
steps.body: If monthly payment savings are positive, the calculator estimates simple break-even months. Also compare total interest over each loan's full term.

sections.heading: Break-even estimate
sections.body: Simple break-even months = closing costs ÷ positive monthly payment savings. If monthly savings are not positive, a simple break-even estimate is not provided.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: This simple break-even calculation does not discount future payments or include every refinancing cost. Total-interest comparison uses each loan's full remaining or new term; terms may differ, and future rate changes or fees can affect the decision.

tools.title: Personal Loan Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Estimate scheduled loan payments, total interest, the effect of an extra monthly payment and the impact of an origination fee deducted from the loan proceeds.

steps.title: Enter the requested loan amount
steps.body: Use the principal amount stated in the loan offer.

steps.title: Enter rate and term
steps.body: Provide the annual interest rate and repayment term.

steps.title: Add fee and optional extra payment
steps.body: Enter the origination-fee percentage and any additional monthly payment. The fee must be below 100%.

steps.title: Review cash received and repayment
steps.body: The calculator estimates the fee, net proceeds, scheduled payment and accelerated repayment schedule.

steps.title: Compare borrowing cost
steps.body: Review total interest plus fee and the estimated fee-adjusted annualized cost.

sections.heading: Fee and annualized-cost estimates
sections.body: Origination fee = requested principal × fee percentage. Net proceeds = principal − fee. Total interest-plus-fee cost = modeled interest + origination fee. The fee-adjusted annualized estimate is derived from net proceeds and scheduled base payments.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: The fee-adjusted annualized figure is an estimate, not a lender's legally disclosed APR. Actual APR may include other charges, payment timing and lender-specific conventions.

tools.title: Student Loan Repayment Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Compare an illustrative fixed-rate student-loan repayment schedule with a scenario that adds an extra monthly payment toward principal.

steps.title: Enter the loan balance
steps.body: Enter the outstanding student-loan principal.

steps.title: Enter the annual rate and term
steps.body: Provide the annual interest rate and repayment period.

steps.title: Enter any extra monthly payment
steps.body: The model assumes the extra amount is applied to principal after the scheduled payment.

steps.title: Calculate the schedules
steps.body: The calculator models standard and accelerated fixed-rate repayment.

steps.title: Compare interest and payoff time
steps.body: Review the estimated interest savings and reduction in repayment months.

sections.heading: Monthly interest
sections.body: Monthly interest is calculated from the opening balance × annual rate ÷ 1,200. The scheduled payment and any extra amount are then applied to the balance.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: This illustration does not model income-driven repayment, government forgiveness, subsidies, deferment, capitalization or jurisdiction-specific rules. Servicer results may differ because of accrual methods, timing and payment-allocation policies.

tools.title: Simple Interest Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Calculate interest on an original principal over a number of days, using a selected 360-, 365- or 366-day year basis. A separate compound-interest comparison is provided for illustration.

steps.title: Enter the principal
steps.body: Enter the original amount on which simple interest will be calculated.

steps.title: Enter the annual rate
steps.body: Provide the annual simple-interest rate as a percentage.

steps.title: Enter the number of days and day basis
steps.body: Choose 360, 365 or 366 as the day-count basis used to convert days into years.

steps.title: Review interest and total
steps.body: The calculator reports simple interest and adds it to principal. It also shows an illustrative annual-compounding comparison.

sections.heading: Formulas
sections.body: Time in years = number of days ÷ selected day-count basis. Simple interest = principal × (annual rate ÷ 100) × time. Total = principal + simple interest.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: Simple interest is calculated on the original principal only. The compound comparison assumes annual compounding and is not part of the simple-interest amount.

tools.title: Retirement Savings Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Project a possible future retirement-savings balance from current savings, monthly contributions, an assumed annual return, a time horizon and an inflation assumption.

steps.title: Enter current savings
steps.body: Use the amount already saved for retirement.

steps.title: Set monthly contributions
steps.body: Enter the amount you plan to contribute at the end of each month.

steps.title: Choose return and time horizon
steps.body: Enter an assumed annual return and the number of years to project.

steps.title: Add an inflation assumption
steps.body: Enter an annual inflation rate to estimate the future balance in today's purchasing-power terms.

steps.title: Calculate the projection
steps.body: The model applies monthly growth to the opening balance and then adds the monthly contribution.

steps.title: Review the projected values
steps.body: Compare future value, total contributions, estimated growth and inflation-adjusted value.

sections.heading: Projection method
sections.body: Each month, interest = opening balance × annual return ÷ 1,200. The monthly contribution is then added at month end. Inflation-adjusted value = projected future value ÷ (1 + inflation rate)^years.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: The calculator assumes a constant return, monthly compounding and end-of-month contributions. Actual investment returns vary and may be negative; fees, taxes, contribution changes and market volatility are not forecast.

tools.title: 401(k) Contribution Calculator Guide
tools.introduction: Estimate how employee contributions and an employer matching contribution could affect a projected 401(k) balance over time. The calculation is illustrative and does not replace plan documents or tax guidance.

steps.title: Enter annual salary
steps.body: Use the salary amount on which your plan calculates contributions and matching.

steps.title: Enter employee contribution percentage
steps.body: Provide the percentage of salary you plan to contribute.

steps.title: Enter employer match terms
steps.body: Enter the employer match percentage and the eligible salary percentage.

steps.title: Enter current balance and assumptions
steps.body: Provide the starting 401(k) balance, assumed annual return and projection period.

steps.title: Calculate monthly contributions
steps.body: The model converts annual employee and employer contributions into monthly amounts and applies monthly growth.

steps.title: Review the projection
steps.body: Compare projected value and contribution totals, including the modeled employer match.

sections.heading: Employer match calculation
sections.body: Annual employee contribution = salary × employee contribution percentage. Eligible match percentage is capped at the lower of employee contribution percentage and eligible salary percentage. Annual employer match = salary × eligible match percentage × employer match percentage.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.body: This illustration does not model annual contribution limits, vesting schedules, fees, taxes or plan-specific rules. Employer matching formulas vary by plan; verify the plan's exact terms.
